newsitem.title: USA: Officials probe E coli infections in Indiana.
newsitem.headline: Officials probe E coli infections in Indiana.

text.p: An apparent outbreak of E coli bacterial infection has left two South Bend boys fighting for their lives and may have struck several other people in northwestern Indiana, health officials said on Wednesday.

While the source of the outbreak has not been identified, the two boys both ate hamburgers at a restaurant, Mazie Martin, director of nurses for the St. Joseph County Health Department said. The restaurant was not identified.
The other possible cases, she said, involved a variety of food sources including chicken, meat bought at a grocery store and ground beef in a spaghetti sauce.

The boys, Jason McKinnies, 2, and his half-brother Cody Edge, 19 months, were in critical but stable condition at an Indianapolis hospital where they were undergoing hourly kidney dialysis, a spokeswoman for the hospital said on Wednesday.

Investigators said two other children in the boys' family showed no signs of infection. State and local health officials said four other people in the South Bend area may also have been infected, although tests are still under way to confirm of E coli was involved.
The two boys were admitted to the Indianapolis hospital last week.
The World Health Organization warned two weeks ago that there has been an increrase in food-borne E coli infections. An outbreak in Scotland last year took 20 lives.
A virulent form of the bacteria identified 15 years ago can get into food by improper slaughtering and hygiene techniques.
